extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, private labelers, legal counsel, and other stakeholders affected by CPSC disclosures; CPSC staff and decisionmakers
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulation describing the Consumer Product Safety Commission's procedures and standards for public disclosure and retraction of information under section 6(b) of the CPSA, including notice and comment, accuracy, fairness, exceptions, and delegation. Guidance is aimed at both Commission staff and firms whose identity may be ascertainable from disclosed information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the rules
rubrics_metrics.description: These rules apply to the public disclosure of any information obtained under the Consumer Product Safety Act (CPSA), the Flammable Fabrics Act (FFA), the Poison Prevention Packaging Act (PPPA), and the Federal Hazardous Substances Act (FHSA), or to be disclosed to the public in connection therewith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic purpose — notice, accuracy, fairness, and retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Set forth CPSC policy and procedure under sections 6(b)(1)-(5) of the CPSA relating to public disclosure of information from which the identity of a manufacturer or private labeler can be readily ascertained, and provide for retraction of inaccurate or misleading information that reflects adversely on safety or practices as required by section 6(b)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirements of section 6(b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to public disclosure of information from which the identity of a manufacturer or private labeler can be readily ascertained, the Commission, to the extent practicable, must provide advance notice and opportunity to comment; take reasonable steps to assure the information is accurate; ensure disclosure is fair in the circumstances and reasonably related to effectuating the purposes of the Acts; and not disclose in fewer than 15 calendar days after notice unless consent or a public health-and-safety finding permits less notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also note that section 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) establish exceptions; section 15(b) creates separate reporting obligations that interact with disclosure limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must establish procedures (section 6(b)(6)) to ensure Commission-initiated disclosures that reflect on product safety are accurate and not misleading, whether or not they would enable the public to readily ascertain a manufacturer's identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information subject to section 6(b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is subject to section 6(b)(1) only if (1) a Commission member, employee, agent, representative, or contractor in an official capacity proposes to disclose it; (2) the manner in which the product is designated or described permits the public to readily ascertain the manufacturer's or private labeler's identity; and (3) the information was obtained, generated, or received under the Acts or is disclosed in connection therewith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1101.12 and §1101.13 for related definitions and tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information not subject to section 6(b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b)(1) requirements do not apply to: information within statutory exceptions in 6(b)(4) or 6(b)(5); information the Commission is required by law to make public; information required to be disclosed to the President or Congress under specified statutes; information filed or presented in administrative proceedings or litigation to which the Commission is a party (unless subject to 6(b)(4)); reports of harm posted pursuant to section 6A; information already public via other sources (if source and use are clearly indicated and not misleading); and information that, in context, does not disclose materially more or different information than previously disclosed by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'public'
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of section 6(b)(1), 'public' includes any person except: Commission members/employees/agents in an official capacity; certain state officials under section 29(a)(2); members of Commission Chronic Hazard Advisory Panels; persons to which the information pertains or who provided the information (and their legal representatives); other federal/state/local/foreign agencies where disclosure is governed by section 29(f); and specified congressional committee members acting pursuant to committee business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even excluded categories' disclosures may still be subject to section 6(b) when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public ability to ascertain readily identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b)(1) applies only when a reasonable person receiving the information in the form to be disclosed and lacking specialized expertise can readily ascertain from the information itself the identity of the manufacturer or private labeler. Information about product categories is not within scope if it will not permit the public to ascertain manufacturers' identities. Information about manufacturers that does not designate/describe a consumer product is also outside the scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an objective 'reasonable person' test focusing on the form in which the information will be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and transmission of notice (oral/written; electronic preferred)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice may be oral or written. The Commission will generally provide written notice and opportunity to comment, except where written notice is impracticable; if impracticable, oral notice will be provided when practicable. The Commission, to the extent practicable, will transmit notice via email or other electronic means; if not practicable or receipt cannot be confirmed, the Commission will use other methods (U.S. mail or other delivery service).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall, to the extent practicable, provide the manufacturer or private labeler with: (1) the actual text of the information to be disclosed or a summary; (2) a general description of the manner of disclosure and any other relevant information intended to be included; (3) a request for comment including a request for explanatory data or other relevant information; (4) a statement that the Commission may, and upon written request shall, include the firm's comments or a summary thereof with the disclosure to the extent permitted; (5) notice that the firm may request confidential treatment under section 6(a)(3); (6) a statement that no further request for comment will be made if the intended disclosure does not disclose materially more or different information than previously disclosed; and (7) the name, contact information, and time when comments are due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for comment — standard and variations
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, manufacturers and private labelers receive 10 calendar days from transmission of notice to furnish comments; those receiving notice by mail get an additional 3 calendar days. The Commission may provide more time for voluminous or complex material, and may publish a finding that public health and safety requires a lesser notice period (see §1101.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for extension of time to comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for extension must be in writing and submitted at least 48 hours before the deadline, except no extension will be granted if the period was shortened by a public health/safety finding (unless the Commission initiates an extension). Requests must explain with specificity why extension is needed and how much time is required. The Commission will respond promptly to extension requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions allowing disclosure in less than 15 days
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may disclose information before the 15-day period expires when (a) the manufacturer/private labeler agrees to an earlier disclosure, notifies the Commission it has no comment, or does not object; or (b) the Commission publishes a finding that the public health and safety requires less than 15 calendar days' notice, for example to warn the public quickly of danger or to correct misleading third-party statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will publish the public health/safety finding in the disclosure itself or elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and sufficiency of comments the Commission seeks
rubrics_metrics.description: The 6(b) opportunity permits firms to furnish information and data that will assist the Commission in evaluating accuracy. A firm's submission must be specific and accompanied by documentation where available to be useful. General comments or allegations that a document is inaccurate or that the Commission did not take reasonable steps are not sufficient. The weight accorded will depend on specificity and completeness; specific comments with documentation receive more weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-specific or general submissions are less likely to affect the Commission's analysis; firms should provide documentation and concrete evidence when contesting accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims of confidentiality for submitted information
rubrics_metrics.description: If a firm believes the information cannot be disclosed because it contains trade secrets or material subject to 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4) (or section 6(a)(2) referencing 18 U.S.C. 1905), the firm may make confidentiality claims when submitting comments. Such claims must identify the specific information and state with specificity the grounds for the claim, consistent with the Commission's FOIA regulation (16 CFR part 1015, particularly 1015.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for nondisclosure of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: If a firm objects to disclosure of its comments or portions thereof, it must notify the Commission at the time of submission and provide the basis for the request. If only portions are objected to, the firm must identify with specificity the portions to be withheld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of intent to disclose after contested inaccuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after following the section 6(b)(1) notice provisions, the Commission determines information claimed to be inaccurate should be disclosed because the Commission believes it has complied with section 6(b)(1), the Commission shall notify the manufacturer or private labeler that it intends to disclose and identify the earliest time it intends to do so. For subjects of a public health and safety finding requiring less than 5 days' notice, the Commission will inform the firm orally or in writing (email preferred where practicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances when notice and opportunity to comment is not practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances include, but are not limited to: (1) when the Commission has taken reasonable steps to ensure the firm is out of business and has no identifiable successor; (2) when information is disclosed in testimony in response to a court order during litigation to which the Commission is not a party; (3) when Commission cannot obtain contact information after a diligent search; and (4) when extraordinary circumstances necessitate immediate disclosure to protect public health and safety while the Commission simultaneously pursues notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule uses a 'to the extent practicable' standard; this list is illustrative rather than exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of manufacturer comments and explanatory statements with disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: In disclosing any information under Subpart D, the Commission may, and upon written request shall, include any comments or other information or a summary submitted by the manufacturer or private labeler to the extent permitted by section 6. The Commission may accompany disclosure with an explanatory statement that makes the nature of the information clear and may include any other relevant information the Commission possesses that places the disclosed information in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: No additional accuracy steps when disclosure does not disclose materially more
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission intends to disclose information not previously disclosed that in context does not disclose materially more or materially different information about the product than previously disclosed in accordance with law, it is not obligated to take additional steps to assure accuracy unless it has reason to question the accuracy of the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable steps to assure disclosure is accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable steps include: (1) investigation by Commission staff or a qualified outside person/entity (e.g., fire marshal, electrical engineer, attending physician) that yields or corroborates the information; (2) Commission staff conducting or obtaining a technical/scientific/other evaluation that yields or corroborates the information; (3) reliance on a statement made under oath or similar enforceable statement; or (4) confirmation by the person who submitted the information, provided the confirmation meets certain listed subconditions (e.g., made by the injured person, eyewitness, qualified investigator, parent/guardian of a child involved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may also include an explanatory statement to assure accuracy. The Commission will review each proposed disclosure susceptible to factual verification to ensure reasonable steps were taken, will consider comments received, and will weigh the specificity and documentation supporting manufacturers' comments when determining whether further investigation is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable steps to assure disclosure is fair in the circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable steps include accompanying disclosures with manufacturer comments (when requested and to the extent permitted), including explanatory statements, and disclosing any other relevant information that assures fairness. The Commission will not disclose information when it determines disclosure would not be fair in the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of disclosures that generally would not be fair: (1) information furnished by a firm to facilitate remedial action or settlement when the firm reasonably expected confidentiality; (2) staff notes/minutes of settlement negotiations and drafts prepared during negotiations where confidentiality was reasonably expected; (3) a manufacturer's comments submitted under section 6(b)(1) when the firm provides a sufficient basis for nondisclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable steps to assure disclosure is reasonably related to effectuating purposes of the Acts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will review whether disclosure is reasonably related to effectuating one or more statutory purposes of the CPSA (sections 2(b) and 5) and those of the FHSA, FFA, and PPPA, and will determine whether the information was prepared/maintained in the course of or to support a Commission activity designed to accomplish one or more statutory purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory exceptions under section 6(b)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exceptions to the requirements of section 6(b)(1)-(3) in 6(b)(4) apply to: (1) information about any consumer product with respect to which the Commission has filed an action under section 12 relating to imminently hazardous products; (2) information about any product the Commission reasonably believes is in violation of any consumer product safety rule or provision of the CPSA or similar provision of another Act enforced by the Commission; and (3) information in the course of or concerning rulemaking, adjudicatory, or other administrative or judicial proceedings under the Acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imminent hazard exception — scope and trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b)(4)(A) provides that section 6(b)(1)-(3) requirements do not apply to public disclosure of information about any consumer product with respect to which the Commission has filed an action under section 12 in a U.S. district court. Once the exception applies, information concerning the product alleged to be imminently hazardous may be disclosed without following section 6(b)(1)-(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 6(b)(4)(A) exception for products believed in violation
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b)(4)(A) also provides that the requirements of section 6(b)(1)-(3) do not apply to public disclosure of information about any consumer product which the Commission has reasonable cause to believe is in violation of any consumer product safety rule or provision of the CPSA or similar rule/provision of any other act enforced by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction requirement for inaccurate or misleading information
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules provide for retraction of inaccurate or misleading information the Commission has disclosed that reflects adversely upon the safety of any product or on the practices of any manufacturer, private labeler, distributor or retailer, as required by section 6(b)(7) of the CPSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart F (listed in table of contents) sets out Commission interpretation and procedure for retraction (see §§1101.51-1101.52).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of authority to General Counsel / appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commission adopted the 6(b) Regulation in 1983, it delegated to the General Counsel the authority to render all decisions concerning release of information subject to section 6(b) when firms have furnished section 6(b) comment, except in certain situations. The Commission determined that a decision by the General Counsel is a final agency decision and is not appealable as of right to the Commission, although the General Counsel may refer an issue to the Commission for decision under §1101.71(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding an additional appeals process on top of the current Commission process would entail additional delay in providing information to the public that is not justified by a countervailing benefit (as stated in the preamble).
